Candidate: Uncertainty-aware graph convolutional neural network for vibrational free‑energy prediction
Type: method

claims [explicit_method_claim]: The presented workflow enables high‑throughput prediction of temperature‑induced solid‑solid phase transitions without performing explicit phonon calculations for each material, dramatically reducing computational cost.

claims [explicit_method_claim]: A graph convolutional neural network predicts vibrational free energies with root‑mean‑square errors of 8.23 meV/atom (training), 11.34 meV/atom (validation) and 12.31 meV/atom (test), and its predictions for MgS and NaH polymorphs match DFT‑computed values across the 200–700 K range.

claims [explicit_method_claim]: Screening of approximately 50 000 inorganic crystals with the machine‑learning model identified over 2 000 temperature‑induced solid‑solid polymorphic transitions between 300 K and 600 K, including 130 stable transitions within the technologically relevant 300 K–350 K interval.

claims [explicit_method_claim]: Several predicted solid‑solid transitions show large entropy changes exceeding 300 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹ (e.g., Li₃MnF₇: 342.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, PnCl₂: 338.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, Fe₄OF₇: 252.1 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹), while the highest entropy changes (> 400 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹) are limited to transitions above 450 K and occur exclusively in nonpolar‑nonpolar categories, reducing their relevance for room‑temperature applications.
